name: Authorization UMG.1 -Grouper/Cluster Tagged Authorization Navigator
description: Walk the Authorization (UM) SOP for the PX_UMG event -the procedure billed on the claim is part of a grouper or cluster table of procedures listed in an authorization, and the billed code is within the same group as the authorized code. Identify the PX_UMG event, confirm the UM Rule ID is not one of the four flagged IDs, confirm the provider is not a Hospital Based Physician, run the eight Claim-Lines exclusion checks, confirm the claim type, read the authorization match result (Case Number NO MATCH), expand the on-file Authorization record and note its procedure code differs from the billed code, prove on the Search → Code Set tab that the billed and authorized procedures share a grouper/cluster, tag that authorization to the claim line, and pay the claim.

steps.name: Review all events and identify the PX_UMG event
steps.description: Review all events in the Event Resolution tab, including informational events, before paying, denying, or routing the claim when multiple events are set. The PX_UMG event will be displayed in the events list -this Authorization event occurs when the procedure billed on the claim is part of a grouper or cluster table of procedures listed in an authorization. The billed procedure code is within the same group as the procedure code authorized, and the tagged authorization is a valid approval of the billed procedure code.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee opens the Event Resolution tab and reviews the events list, where the PX_UMG event is shown.
steps.hint: Open 'Event Resolution' and review the events list. The active PX_UMG event is shown -the billed procedure is part of a grouper/cluster table of procedures listed in an authorization.
steps.checklistItem: Review all events and identify the PX_UMG event

steps.name: Check the UM Rule ID
steps.description: Determine whether the UM Rule ID is one of MMS001, PSYCH001, ASCRULE01, or NYSTATE02 by navigating to the Claim Data tab, then the Review sub-tab, and expanding the Utilization Management section. Review the UM Detail Service table, which contains the Line #, Procedure, Revenue Code, Date, Rule ID, and Case Number columns, and identify the value displayed in the Rule ID column. If the Rule ID matches any of the specified values (MMS001, PSYCH001, ASCRULE01, or NYSTATE02), follow the alternate SOP steps. If none of these Rule IDs are present, proceed to the next step. In this scenario, the Rule ID is AIMREHAB, which does not match any of the specified values; therefore, the trainee may proceed to the next step.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee opens the Review sub-tab inside Claim Data and reads the UM Detail Service table's Rule ID.
steps.hint: Open 'Claim Data' → 'Review' and expand Utilization management. The UM Detail Service Rule ID is AIMREHAB -not one of MMS001 / PSYCH001 / ASCRULE01 / NYSTATE02 -so proceed.

steps.name: Check for a Hospital Based Physician
steps.description: Verify whether the provider billed on the claim qualifies as a Hospital Based Physician by navigating to the Provider Information tab, then the Rendering section, and reviewing the Specialty Description field. A provider is considered a Hospital Based Physician if the Specialty Description is Anesthesiology, Radiology, Emergency Room Physician, Pathology, Assistant Surgeon, Neonatology, Intensivist, or Hospitalist. If the provider is identified as a Hospital Based Physician, follow the alternate SOP steps. If the provider does not fall within one of these specialties, proceed to the next step. In this scenario, the Specialty Description is Cardiology; therefore, the provider is not considered a Hospital Based Physician, and the trainee may proceed to the next step.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee opens the Provider Information tab to read the Rendering Speciality Description.
steps.hint: Open 'Provider Info' and read the Speciality description under Rendering -it is Cardiology, not a Hospital Based Physician specialty, so proceed.
steps.checklistItem: Check for a Hospital Based Physician

steps.name: Run the Claim Lines exclusion checks
steps.description:
On the Claim Lines tab, check eight exclusion conditions against the claim line. For this claim, the line shows Procedure 97530, Modifier "—", and POS 21.

For each check, if the condition matches, follow the alternate SOP steps. Otherwise, proceed to the next check.
Consulting Physician -Procedure code is 99231–99233 or 99251–99255. (97530 → no match)

Modifier 26 -Modifiers field equals 26. ("—" → no match)

Implants -Procedure code starts with C or L. (97530 → no match)

PAP / CPAP / BIPAP machines or supplies -Procedure code starts with E. (97530 → no match)

Chiropractic with PT, or PT alone -Procedure code is A2000–A2999. (97530 → no match)

Emergency Room or Urgent Care -POS is 23 (ER) or 20 (Urgent Care). (21 → no match)

Ambulance services -POS is 41 or 42. (21 → no match)

Drug administration -Procedure code is J0000–J8999. (97530 → no match)
In this scenario, none of the eight conditions match, so the trainee proceeds.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee opens the Claim Lines tab to run the eight exclusion checks against the Procedure, Modifiers, and POS fields.
steps.hint: Open 'Claim Lines'. Procedure 97530 (not 99231–99255 / C / L / E / A2xxx / J-code), Modifier '-' (not 26), and POS 21 (not 23/20/41/42) -none of the eight exclusions match, so proceed.
steps.checklistItem: Run the Claim Lines exclusion checks

steps.name: Check the claim type against the SOP table
steps.description: Determine whether the claim falls under a scenario defined in the UM Events Authorization SOP by navigating to the Claim Data tab, then the Details sub-tab, and reviewing the Claim Type field. Compare the Claim Type value against the scenarios listed in the UM Events Authorization SOP table. If the value matches a scenario in the table, follow the corresponding SOP instructions for that scenario. If the value does not match any listed scenario, proceed to the next step. In this scenario, the Claim Type is Professional, which does not correspond to a scenario requiring special handling; therefore, the trainee may proceed to the next step.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee opens the Details sub-tab inside Claim Data to read the claim type.
steps.hint: Open 'Claim Data' → 'Details' and read the claim type -it is Professional, which is not one of the SOP-table scenarios, so proceed.
steps.checklistItem: Check the claim type against the SOP table

steps.name: Verify the authorization match
steps.description: Verify whether a matching authorization exists for the claim line(s) requiring authorization by navigating to the Claim Data tab, then the Review sub-tab, and expanding the Utilization Management section. Review the UM Detail Service table and examine the Case Number column for the applicable claim line(s). A valid Case Number indicates that a matching authorization exists. A value of NO MATCH indicates that an authorization exists but does not correspond to the billed service. A blank Case Number field indicates that no authorization exists. In this scenario, the Case Number field displays NO MATCH, indicating that an authorization exists but does not correspond to the service billed on the claim. Therefore, the trainee may proceed to review the authorization record, and will tag it to the claim line once the shared grouper is proved.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee opens the Review sub-tab inside Claim Data and reads the UM Detail Service table's Case Number.
steps.hint: Open 'Claim Data' → 'Review' and read the Case Number in the UM Detail Service table -it shows NO MATCH (an authorization exists but does not match the billed service), so review the authorization record.

steps.name: Expand the authorization and identify the PX_UMG scenario
steps.description: Expand the Authorization section by navigating to the Claim Data tab, then the Review sub-tab. Review the authorization record, which displays the Authorization #, Date Range, Procedure, Provider, Status, Svc Type, and Score fields. Select the chevron (>) icon, or click the authorization row, to expand the authorization details inline. Compare the Procedure code billed on the claim with the Procedure code listed on the authorization. In this scenario, the billed procedure code is 97530 and the authorized procedure code is 97110. This discrepancy is the condition that triggered the PX_UMG event. However, an authorization may still be considered valid if both procedure codes belong to the same grouper/cluster. Therefore, the trainee should proceed to the Code Set tab to verify whether the billed and authorized procedure codes are included within the same grouper.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee expands the Authorization row (which dispatches the expand_authorization action) and notes the authorized Procedure 97110 differs from the billed 97530.
steps.hint: On 'Claim Data' → 'Review', click the chevron on the Authorization row to expand it. The authorized Procedure is 97110, which differs from the billed 97530 -proceed to the Code Set tab to confirm both share a grouper/cluster.
steps.checklistItem: Expand the authorization and identify the PX_UMG scenario

steps.name: Search the billed code and view its grouper/clusters
steps.description: Navigate to the Search tab, then the Code Set sub-tab, and review the Search Codesets section. In the Select Code Type field, select Procedure Code (Px). Enter the billed procedure code 97530 in the Enter Code field, enter 04/28/2025 in both the Service From and Service To fields, and then click Search to display the codeset information. Next, expand the UM Grouper/Cluster section and review the Grouper/Cluster Details table, which contains the Grouper/Cluster Code, State Code, From Date, and Thru Date columns. In this scenario, procedure code 97530 is associated with two grouper/cluster codes: 0024 (ALL, 01/01/2000, 12/31/2099) and 0155 (ALL, 03/25/2019, 12/31/2099). This indicates that procedure code 97530 belongs to both groupers/clusters
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee searches the billed code 97530 on the Code Set sub-tab (which dispatches the search_codeset action) and the UM Grouper/Cluster Details table reveals groupers 0024 and 0155.
steps.hint: Open 'Search' → 'Code Set'. Select Procedure Code (Px), enter 97530, set Service from/to 04/28/2025, and click Search. Expand UM Grouper/Cluster -97530 belongs to groupers 0024 and 0155.
steps.checklistItem: Search the billed code and view its grouper/clusters

steps.name: Confirm both procedures belong to the same grouper/cluster
steps.description: Select the first grouper (0024) -the List of Codes section expands with five fields (Procedure code, Cluster/Grouper code, State code, From date, To date). The first three rows show procedure codes 97110, 90912, and 90913, all belonging to Cluster/Grouper code 0024 with State code All, From date 1/1/00, and Thru date 12/31/99. This confirms that the authorized procedure 97110 belongs to the same group (0024) as the billed procedure 97530, so the authorization for 97110 can be tagged to the billed code 97530 and the claim is payable.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee selects grouper 0024 (which dispatches the select_grouper action) and the List of Codes table reveals the authorized procedure 97110.
steps.hint: Select grouper 0024 in the Grouper/Cluster Details table. The List of Codes for 0024 contains 97110 -the authorized procedure shares the same group as the billed 97530, so the claim is payable.
steps.checklistItem: Confirm both procedures belong to the same grouper/cluster

steps.name: Tag the correct authorization to the claim line
steps.description: Tag the correct authorization in the Case Number field of the UM Detail Service sub-section under the Utilization management section. A radio button (circle button) appears at the start of each authorization row; click the radio button on the first authorization row (UM97608093), and a Tag button will appear. Click the Tag button to move the Authorization # of that row into the Case Number field of the Utilization management section, replacing the existing NO MATCH value. With the correct authorization tagged, the trainee can now proceed to pay the claim.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee selects the authorization row's radio and clicks Tag (which dispatches the tag_authorization action), moving UM97608093 into the Case Number cell and replacing NO MATCH.
steps.hint: Click the radio on the authorization row (UM97608093), then click the Tag button. The Case Number cell changes from NO MATCH to UM97608093.
steps.checklistItem: Tag the correct authorization to the claim line

steps.name: Submit Pay decision
steps.description: Navigate to the Decision section in the header, select 'Pay' from the dropdown menu and click Submit.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee confirms the Pay decision in the submit dialog.
steps.hint: Pick 'Pay' from the Decision dropdown in the claim header, then click Submit and confirm in the dialog.

Provider is not a Hospital Based Physician (Cardiology)
